title: The Lens — rich
forward_vector: I am the manifest of The Lens's rich face, its first round, a Study and still a proposal: two walks that each start from one idea and end on a test of the page's own claim (move the glass over four of the page's paragraphs, read live, until three hidden rules are judged blind; and the [L]ens picker's ranking on the real typed-link graph, until two hops turns out to hold four tenths of the palace), beside the two Daily Page proofs that set the bar and the two sketches the text already names. I grow when the page is enriched again; I never hold the entry's words.

offers.what: 'Already-linked or two-hop-apart pages are reliable sparks; distant unlinked pages are mostly noise.' The sentence entered on 2026-06-09 (c79de58f), before any spark score existed, and the evidence since is thin: the three-pair July prototype the code cites (lens-suggest.js:8-11) had no two-hop pair, so 'two-hop-apart' has never been measured. On the live graph of 2026-11-03 (328 entries, 2490 typed links, walked as the [L]ens picker walks it), one hop holds 4.2% of the palace for the average entry; two hops hold 41.0% (median 39.4%, from 11.9% to 96.3%); no pair of entries is unreachable, and the farthest apart any two sit is 5 hops. So one hop is a filter and two hops is not, and 'distant unlinked' can only mean three or more hops. The nine scores on record by distance: 1 hop 5, 4, 3; 2 hops 3.5, 1.5 (both hand-written); 3 hops 1.5, 3.5, 4. Offer: say the claim came before its evidence, that one hop is the filter and two hops is most of the palace, and hold 'reliable sparks' until the lensings the forward vector asks for are in.

'The nearest candidates render as clickable chips ("nearest on the graph")'. The ranking is hop count alone, and lens-suggest.js breaks a tie by title (a.distance − b.distance || a.title.localeCompare(b.title)). For The Lens, 21 entries tie at one hop and the eight chips are the first eight of them A to Z (Agent Wellbeing through Meaning and the Link). Offer: one clause saying ties break alphabetically, so within a ring the chips are the alphabet's pick; it bears on the Open Question about the right suggestion algorithm.

'Move the glass to a new patch (or swap the lens) and the reading must change in a way specific to that text.' A rule that only fills a fixed template with each paragraph's own words changes on every paragraph, so it passes 'must change'; 'specific to that text' carries the whole test. The procedure's self-check already names this failure ('did I deploy my real apparatus, or borrow A's vocabulary?'). Offer: join the two in this section's test sentence, so the change that counts is in what the glass brings, not the words it borrows. This rests on reading, not on the piece's meter: the borrower sits beside the formula once each paragraph's words are taken out (0.93 and 0.88 against 0.96 and 0.93) by construction, since its only other words are its fixed template, so the meter shows the definition rather than finding it.

verdicts.why: A real test: two hops could have come out a short list and came out 41% of the palace; my own BFS on the snapshot gets the same 4% / 41% / 0 unreachable / 5 hops, and the walk climbs from one entry's links to every entry. Note: the two July scores it calls inferred (1.5, 3.5) are on record in _ops/scratch/lens-prototype-2026-07-02.md:27,37, so cite that and drop 'inferred'.

Fix: match lengths and openings, state chance and the rule first, tally several trials (record has the detail).

pieces.title: move the glass · a walk in six steps
pieces.caption: **The test in your hand, on this page's own words.** Four paragraphs of The Lens, read live, under a glass you drag: Simondon, the Trickster and Ohm's Law, each in its own register with a distortion check; then a glass that says the same thing everywhere and one that only borrows the paragraph's words; last, one glass with three hidden rules over three trials, chance and the verdict rule stated before the first. The three readings match in length within 8% and open alike: marking by length alone scored 3.25 of 9 over 40 headless sessions, where luck averages 3.
